notes.headline: Guangdong does it again; Blocktopus bounces back
notes.dek: The champs had the best line in the league for the second straight week. Blocktopus beat eweiss35 6–3 behind Wembanyama's 120 points and 42 rebounds.
notes.byline: Written from Fantrax league data for Week 2 (Oct 26 – Nov 1).

storylines.title: Two weeks, 22 all-play wins
storylines.body: Guangdong beat Competing God 6–3 and would have beaten all 11 teams again, with league highs in threes (105) and steals (71) and 890 points. Doncic (139 points) and Mobley made the Pro-Am Starting 5. They're one of four 2–0 teams.

storylines.title: Wemby's week
storylines.body: Victor Wembanyama was the league's top player: 120 points and 42 rebounds on 52.6% shooting. Blocktopus beat eweiss35 6–3 with the league's best FG% (.493), winning rebounds, steals, blocks, turnovers and FT% too.

storylines.title: Presti does everything but win
storylines.body: Sam Presti led the league in assists (230) and blocks (40) and would have beaten 9 teams, but lost 5–4 to LeBrown James, who scored a league-high 897 points. Presti's 128 turnovers were the most in the league.

storylines.title: Rookie watch
storylines.body: Caleb Wilson topped the rookies again (84 points, 23 rebounds, 8 steals, 5 blocks). Teammate Darius Acuff scored 116, and Cameron Boozer pulled down 37 rebounds for Competing God.

storylines.title: Brown Shirt Chucker
storylines.body: Naz Reid (Shanghai) went 23 of 68 from the field for 64 points. Shanghai still beat Zach Babies 7–2.

bruno.auysoygrmqqv88in: Down a spot to third, but nothing changed in the core: Flagg, Peterson and Wagler all turn 23 in the title season, with four picks still to come.
bruno.d91prsm4mqqv88in: Up to second. Darius Acuff and Caleb Wilson are off to fast starts, and with Dylan Harper all three are 24 or younger in 2030–31. Their projected strength climbs every season.
bruno.070oazg4mqqv88in: Still No. 1, and now first today too. Doncic is 31 in the title season, with Trey Murphy (30) and Santi Aldama (29) still in their primes. The only team in the top two on both lists.
bruno.b33iacngmqqv88in: Holding at fourth. Wembanyama (26 in the title season) is the league's best long-term piece, and Sabonis helps now, but no picks remain to add depth around him.
bruno.saydaqzgmqqv88in: Sixth, with eight picks, the second-most in the league. AJ Dybantsa, VJ Edgecombe and LaMelo Ball are the core, and their strength rises every season.
bruno.mizl2op8mqqv88im: Up to seventh. Shai is 32 in the title season, but Moussa Diabate and Kyshawn George give them younger pieces. Third today, so the window is still now.
bruno.ygisq4rlmqqv88in: Fifth. Maxey anchors it, but Tatum (32) and Donovan Mitchell (34) will be on the back nine by 2030–31, so the line stays flat.
bruno.xoe774vlmqqv88in: Down to tenth. Second-best roster today, but Jokic is 35, Murray 33 and Bane 32 in the title season. Their strength falls every year.
bruno.cipchrpimqqv88in: Ninth. Amen Thompson and Dyson Daniels (both 27 in 2030–31) are the base; the veterans around them age out, so the line drifts down.
bruno.rufupenmmqqv88in: Up three spots to eighth. Cameron Boozer (23 in the title season) and Morez Johnson are a real young base, but their strength fades as the veterans age.
bruno.ctvglb6gmqqv88in: Last on the long view. Porter and Reaves are 32 and Brunson 34 in the title season, and they hold no picks.
bruno.n3z2eshxmqqv88in: Up to eleventh. Ten picks, the most in the league, but no young core yet beyond Nate Ament. Expect a big climb once those picks become players.
